module-0-welcome-board-project.label: Module Project: Build a Welcome Board
module-0-welcome-board-project.summary: Build one Python welcome board in stages. Preserve working code while adding a useful comment, literals, an arithmetic expression, and a final welcome message.

sketch0.title: Build one program, one improvement at a time

mp-1-set-event-title.title: Set the event title
mp-1-set-event-title.prompt:
Start the welcome board with one line that prints exactly:

`Code Club Open House`
mp-1-set-event-title.hint: Use one `print()` call with the title as a string literal.

help.concept: The project begins with one working line. Later stages will keep this line and extend the same program.
help.hint_1: The event title is text, so write it as a quoted string.
help.hint_2: This stage needs one output line only.

mp-1-set-event-title.starterCode: # Start the board with the event title.

0.message: Start with one print call for the exact event title.

mp-2-add-useful-comment.title: Document the board
mp-2-add-useful-comment.prompt:
Keep the working title line. Add one useful Python comment on the line above it describing the purpose of the program.

The program output must still be exactly:

`Code Club Open House`
mp-2-add-useful-comment.hint: A Python comment starts with `#` and should not become output.

help.concept: Comments document code for readers without changing the program's normal output.
help.hint_1: Put the comment above the existing `print()` call.
help.hint_2: Do not add another printed line in this stage.

mp-2-add-useful-comment.solutionCode:
# Show the welcome board for arriving students
print("Code Club Open House")

0.message: Add one non-empty Python comment above the existing event-title print call.

mp-3-add-event-time.title: Add the event time
mp-3-add-event-time.prompt:
Keep the comment and title. Add one new output line under the title that prints exactly:

`Doors open at 4 PM`
mp-3-add-event-time.hint: Preserve the existing program and add one new `print()` call below the title.

help.concept: A cumulative project grows by preserving correct code and adding one focused improvement.
help.hint_1: The comment stays at the top.
help.hint_2: The new time line should appear after the event title.

mp-3-add-event-time.starterCode:
# Show the welcome board for arriving students
print("Code Club Open House")
mp-3-add-event-time.solutionCode:
# Show the welcome board for arriving students
print("Code Club Open House")
print("Doors open at 4 PM")

0.message: Preserve the comment and title, then add the event-time line below them.

mp-4-add-seat-literal.title: Add a numeric literal
mp-4-add-seat-literal.prompt:
Keep the board so far. Add these two output lines at the bottom:

`Seats available`
`24`

Print `24` as a numeric literal, not as quoted text.
mp-4-add-seat-literal.hint: The label is a string, but the seat count should be the number `24` without quotes.

help.concept: A numeric literal is a number written directly in code. Quoting `24` would turn it into a string instead.
help.hint_1: Use one print call for the label and one for the number.
help.hint_2: The line for the count should contain `print(24)`, not `print("24")`.

mp-4-add-seat-literal.starterCode:
# Show the welcome board for arriving students
print("Code Club Open House")
print("Doors open at 4 PM")
mp-4-add-seat-literal.solutionCode:
# Show the welcome board for arriving students
print("Code Club Open House")
print("Doors open at 4 PM")
print("Seats available")
print(24)

0.message: Preserve the board and print the seat count as numeric literal 24 without quotes.

mp-5-calculate-helper-count.title: Calculate the helper count
mp-5-calculate-helper-count.prompt:
Keep everything already working. Add these two output lines:

`Helpers ready`
`6`

Do not type the final `6` directly. Make Python calculate it with the expression `2 * 3`.
mp-5-calculate-helper-count.hint: Print the label first, then print the expression `2 * 3` on the next line.

help.concept: An arithmetic expression produces a value. Here the program should calculate the helper count rather than hard-code the result.
help.hint_1: Keep `2 * 3` visible in the source code.
help.hint_2: The expression should not be inside quotes.

mp-5-calculate-helper-count.starterCode:
# Show the welcome board for arriving students
print("Code Club Open House")
print("Doors open at 4 PM")
print("Seats available")
print(24)
mp-5-calculate-helper-count.solutionCode:
# Show the welcome board for arriving students
print("Code Club Open House")
print("Doors open at 4 PM")
print("Seats available")
print(24)
print("Helpers ready")
print(2 * 3)

0.message: Preserve the board and calculate the helper count with the expression 2 * 3.

mp-6-add-final-message.title: Finish the welcome board
mp-6-add-final-message.prompt:
Keep the complete working board from the previous step. Add one final line at the bottom that prints exactly:

`Bring your questions!`

Preserve every earlier line and add only the new final message.
mp-6-add-final-message.hint: Start from the working program exactly as it is and add one quoted string in a new `print()` call at the bottom.

help.concept: A cumulative project grows from the previous working solution. The final step should preserve all earlier behavior and add only the new requirement.
help.hint_1: Do not rewrite or remove any of the earlier board lines.
help.hint_2: The final value is text, so keep it inside matching quotes.

mp-6-add-final-message.starterCode:
# Show the welcome board for arriving students
print("Code Club Open House")
print("Doors open at 4 PM")
print("Seats available")
print(24)
print("Helpers ready")
print(2 * 3)
mp-6-add-final-message.solutionCode:
# Show the welcome board for arriving students
print("Code Club Open House")
print("Doors open at 4 PM")
print("Seats available")
print(24)
print("Helpers ready")
print(2 * 3)
print("Bring your questions!")

sketch-1.title: Build one program, one improvement at a time
sketch-1.bodyMarkdown:
A club leader needs a simple welcome board for the first Python meetup.

This project is one continuous program, not a collection of unrelated exercises. Each stage starts from working code and adds one new requirement.

By the end, your board will combine several Module 0 skills:

- display text with `print()`
- keep a useful comment for readers
- use a numeric literal as a real number
- calculate a value with an arithmetic expression
- use an error message to make a targeted debugging fix
- preserve earlier working behavior while the program grows

Treat every completed stage as a version worth keeping. When the next requirement arrives, change only what needs to change.
